header:
# Progress — run `agent-harness-2026-11-07` (agent-harness)

What this file is: the run's journal, rendered from `entries.jsonl`, newest entry first. Each entry is one session's own account: what it built, what it verified, what failed. The feature list (`feature_list.json` in this directory) has one milestone, S4 of the slim-suite spec (`docs/specs/2026-11-03-slim-suite.md`): the bash decision logic that burns the suite moves into pure `.mjs` functions with a unit test per branch, no note text changed, no check removed (the brief's Decision 16 (b)). Five features: S4-01 plans the moves, S4-02 the suite runner's decisions (`lib/check.sh` → `lib/checkdecide.mjs`), S4-03 the lane's verdict and exit table and how a run ends (`lib/lane.sh`, `lib/driver.sh` → `lib/lane.mjs`), S4-04 the queue entry format and INBOX status parsers (`lib/queue.mjs`, `lib/inbox.mjs`), S4-05 the review with the proofs, the forty mutants and the Predictions table (the after row and the solo CPU and wall rows wait for an empty box after the run). `passes` on a feature means its session's fast tier was green and its steps were done; the milestone is verified independently and merged into `main` when all five pass. Steer from the phone: edit `INBOX.md` on this branch (first line `status: pause` or `status: stop`; answers under `## Answers`).

discoveries.text: Two checks count treekey.mjs starts (partial-key 'one treekey start', resident-helper-ask's check_run pair), so treekey.mjs stays its own question: check.sh asks checkdecide.mjs before as a second one, and check_run hands that answer in HARNESS_CHECK_BEFORE through ask, so a lane's call starts no more node. checkdecide.mjs joins SERVED too.

The second note proof compares from note " to the END of the line, so a line holding a note keeps its trailing code byte for byte: the three end-block lines keep ends+=(…), so runEnd answers lists and bash still builds the reason.

spec_entry in lib/spec.sh is a fifth queue decoder the feature list doesn't name; the plan moves it with S4-04 (default). No check holds a 0x1f byte today: grep -rl x1f tests/checks tests/unit prints nothing.

bash read fails at end of file on a last line with no newline, so closedLane must answer 'lane exited unexpectedly' for an exit file with no final newline; rule 4 of the plan lists the others (read's trim, [[:space:]] against \s, [[:alnum:]], ${w:0:200}).

Only literal-04 of S1's forty lies in an emptied function. In bash it was equivalent (any non-zero refuses), so partialPlan answers the refusing row and the mutant at its new home is row 8 to row 9, which the unit test must catch.

questions: The bash-removed row of the spec's Predictions (150 or more) is on course to miss: the plan's reading gives about 90 to 110 gross, with candidates 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 in three builds. Accept the miss (the default: the final number and this reason go in the decision file at S4-05), or add a fourth build for the debrief's parse and the marker regex (candidates 2 and 7, about 35 lines and more)? discoveries.text: bin/harness is set -e, unlike lib/*.sh: was=$(node … exit 3) ends it silently (stop-records caught it); write x=$(…) || { (( $? == 3 )) && …; }

`harness queue add --continue` replacing a queued entry writes the format itself (printf in cmd_queue), raw: a multi-line option reads back as several arguments. A base-tree bug, left because this move changes no queue byte; asked below.
Node decodes argv and files as UTF-8, so a queue argument that isn't valid UTF-8 no longer keeps its bytes (U+FFFD); marked default in the decision file.
If node fails at the runner's decode, the entry goes to done/ with a failed start logged (mapfile from the file couldn't fail); recoverable by hand, no guard added.
String.replace in an edit script expands $' in the replacement text (it ate a check file once): use a function replacement when editing bash through node.

questions: Should `harness queue add --continue` replacing a queued entry write through lib/queue.mjs, so a multi-line --brief in a repeated request stays one argument? Default: left as it is, because this move changes no queue byte; the fix is one line plus a check.
